coverageGaps.reason: ships 1,500+ deterministic rules and 100 LLM rules — unobservable via CLI (pending review). The claim asserts a SPLIT (deterministic vs LLM) and `truecourse rules list`'s promised output — `Rules for <repo>: N shown (E enabled, D disabled)` plus per-rule rows of key / status / [domain/severity] / language support / name — carries no deterministic-vs-LLM label. Asserting only the total (>1,600 rows) would be a green that does not prove its claim, exactly the defect class the fidelity judge exists to catch. Two ways out, both for the user to choose: label the kind in `rules list` output, or narrow the doc claim.

Code Quality rule counts — unobservable via CLI (pending review) — same as `ships-1500-deterministic-and-100-llm-rules`; additionally an exact count that drifts with every rule added, so a passing assertion would fail on the next rule PR.

the per-file budget defaults to 30 seconds — unobservable via CLI (pending review). Nothing prints the effective budget, so the only proof is a wall-clock measurement: a file that must survive 29s and be skipped at 31s. That is a minutes-long, machine-speed dependent scenario — the flakiness it buys is worse than the coverage. The override claim (`TRUECOURSE_DET_FILE_TIMEOUT_MS`) IS carried, in `survive-a-file-that-exceeds-the-per-file-budget`.

C# is supported with the .NET 8 SDK — needs dotnet-sdk. A supplied dependency with no registered instance: the .NET 8 SDK plus the Roslyn host built from the TrueCourse source tree. Register one and this becomes a flow (seed a `.cs` file, assert a violation against it) — the scenario is blocked, not impossible.

C# semantic rules need the Roslyn host built once — needs dotnet-sdk, and the documented build command (`dotnet build -c Release tools/csharp-roslyn-host`) points INSIDE the TrueCourse source tree, which a user who installed from npm does not have. Blocked on both the supplied SDK and a doc/interface answer to "where does an installed user build the host from".

disabling a rule removes its detection and LLM cost — llm-cost plus an unassertable comparison. The falsifiable half is "the run's LLM call/token totals DROP after the rule is disabled", which needs two full LLM runs over the same project and a comparison BETWEEN their summaries; a scenario asserts per-step matchers, not deltas across steps, and the model's own output is not deterministic enough to assert the rule's absence directly.

.truecourseignore also narrows spec scan doc discovery — out of the authored interface set — the proof runs through `truecourse spec scan` and `.truecourse/specs/corpus.json`, and no `cli/spec` interface exists in reference/interfaces (the reference covers the code-analysis surface: analyze, add, list, rules, hooks, root). It also needs an LLM transport for a full scan. The claim belongs to a spec-scan area flow once that surface's interfaces are authored.

--llm runs the LLM rules for this run — blocked-on the supplied `llm-transport` dependency: proving that an LLM rule RAN needs a live transport, which the reference corpus binds only where the flow is about the transport itself.

--llm pre-approves the cost estimate — blocked-on the supplied `llm-transport` dependency: the cost estimate is only reachable on a run that would really call the model, and its absence must be observed on a terminal.

--llm-transport picks how the LLM is reached for this run — blocked-on the supplied `llm-transport` dependency, and partly unrealizable: the doc's value set includes `agent`, which the post-Phase-0 target deletes (interface decision `phase-0-transport`), so one of the three documented values has no supported path to test.

--io sets the mailbox dir for the agent transport — unrealizable against the post-Phase-0 target: `--io` exists only to serve `--llm-transport agent`, which Phase 0 removes (interface decision `phase-0-transport`). The doc row is drift and is reported as such rather than tested.

--install-skills installs the Claude Code skills without prompting — unrealizable through the reference recipe: the bundled skills tree is copied next to the entrypoint only by the distributable build, while the recipe builds with `pnpm run build` and invokes `tools/cli/dist/index.js`, so there is no skills bundle for the flag to install and the flag is a silent no-op. Realizing it needs a recipe that builds and invokes the published artifact.

add takes --install-skills — unrealizable through the reference recipe: same cause as `cli-ref-analyze-install-skills-installs-without-prompting` — the entrypoint the recipe builds carries no bundled skills tree, so the flag installs nothing and a scenario would assert against an artifact of the build shape rather than against the product.

TRUECOURSE_HOME relocates the per-user directory — unrealizable under the runner's isolation rule: proving the relocation means asserting on the relocated directory, and the only tree a scenario may assert files in is its working tree — which is exactly where a tool home must never point. The runner already relocates the home for every scenario, so the behavior is exercised everywhere and observed nowhere.
TRUECOURSE_LLM_TRANSPORT overrides the saved transport for one run — blocked-on the supplied `llm-transport` dependency: the override is only observable on a run that really reaches the model.
TRUECOURSE_MODEL overrides the model globally — blocked-on the supplied `llm-transport` dependency, and unobservable on the CLI surface: no command prints which model a stage resolved to.
TRUECOURSE_MODEL_<STAGE> overrides the model for one stage — blocked-on the supplied `llm-transport` dependency, and unobservable on the CLI surface: no command prints a per-stage model resolution.
TRUECOURSE_FALLBACK_MODEL is used when the primary is overloaded — unrealizable: the trigger is the provider returning "overloaded", which the corpus cannot cause without faulting a live provider.
TRUECOURSE_MAX_CONCURRENCY caps concurrent LLM calls across stages — blocked-on the supplied `llm-transport` dependency, and unobservable on the CLI surface: in-flight call counts are never printed.

the concurrency cap defaults to min(cpus, 4) — unobservable on the CLI surface, and machine-dependent: the default is a function of the host's CPU count, so any assertion would encode the machine that ran it.
TRUECOURSE_MAX_CONCURRENCY also caps the guard runner's parallel sandboxes — blocked-on layer 2 (no `cli/guard` interface) and unobservable: the sandbox count is never printed.
TRUECOURSE_MAX_API_CONCURRENCY caps resident api-driver servers — blocked-on layer 2 (no `cli/guard` interface) and unobservable: the resident-server count is never printed.
the api-driver server cap defaults to min(TRUECOURSE_MAX_CONCURRENCY, 3) — blocked-on layer 2 (no `cli/guard` interface) and unobservable: the derived default is never printed.

TRUECOURSE_LLM_TIMEOUT_SCALE multiplies every per-call timeout on every transport — blocked-on the supplied `llm-transport` dependency, and unobservable: per-call timeouts are never printed, so proving the multiplication means provoking a timeout at a known duration.
TRUECOURSE_LLM_LOG and TRUECOURSE_LLM_DUMP enable per-call LLM logging — blocked-on the supplied `llm-transport` dependency: with no LLM call there is no per-call log to write.

TRUECOURSE_DET_FILE_TIMEOUT_MS sets the deterministic scan's per-file budget — already realized as an observation by the flow `survive-a-file-that-exceeds-the-per-file-budget`, authored from analyze/overview.mdx. The cli.mdx restatement is kept as its own claim (the cross-doc rule) but is recorded uncovered rather than re-executed: a second scenario would pay for the same pathological-file run to observe the same thing under a different anchor.

the deterministic per-file budget defaults to 30000 ms — already realized as an observation by the flow `survive-a-file-that-exceeds-the-per-file-budget`, authored from analyze/overview.mdx; recorded uncovered here rather than re-executed, for the same reason as `cli-ref-env-det-file-timeout-sets-the-per-file-budget`.

TRUECOURSE_ROSLYN_HOST points at a prebuilt C# Roslyn host binary — blocked-on the supplied `dotnet-sdk` dependency and on a prebuilt host binary the corpus does not build; the C# host claims are realized once, from analyze/overview.mdx.

TRUECOURSE_NO_PRICE_FETCH skips the model-price fetch — unobservable on the CLI surface: skipping the price fetch changes no printed output and no file in the working tree — the evidence is a network request that did not happen.

TRUECOURSE_TELEMETRY=0 opts out of telemetry — unobservable on the CLI surface: the evidence is a network request that did not happen. Every scenario in this corpus sets the variable, so the behavior is relied on everywhere and observed nowhere.
the CLAUDE_CODE_* variables tune Claude Code mode — blocked-on the supplied `claude-code-binary` dependency, and unobservable: none of the five settings is echoed by any command.

Code Analysis shows the architecture graph — Blocked-on a locatable graph surface: the canvas is a ReactFlow region whose nodes, edges, minimap and pane carry no role and no accessible name, and the §10.3 locator policy refuses to guess at one (transform gap G76). Its zoom controls are named, but asserting them would prove a toolbar is mounted, not that the architecture graph rendered. It becomes a flow when the graph region is nameable.

The falsifiable half — the saved credentials are byte-identical after a dashboard session — is worth a flow once a transport is bound, and it still would not prove the universal.

dashboard starts and opens the dashboard — Blocked-on a long-running-process verb the cli driver does not have: `truecourse dashboard` serves until it is stopped, and it OPENS a browser on the user’s machine — a side effect a sandbox must never take. The runner boots the dashboard through the recipe’s own `web.serve`, which is the same server binary the command spawns but not the command itself.

dashboard --reconfigure re-prompts for the run mode — Blocked-on the same long-running-process verb: the re-prompt is followed by the command serving or installing a service, neither of which a step can leave behind.
dashboard --service runs as a background service — Unrealizable in a sandbox: the service mode installs a launchd/systemd unit on the machine, which is state outside the sandbox by definition.
dashboard --service skips the mode prompt — Blocked-on the same service installation — the flag’s prompt-skipping half is only observable on a run that goes on to install the service.
dashboard --console runs in this terminal — Blocked-on the long-running-process verb: the command holds the terminal until it is stopped, so a step that runs it never returns.
dashboard --console skips the mode prompt — Blocked-on the same long-running-process verb.
dashboard stop stops the dashboard — Blocked-on the same long-running-process verb: stopping is only observable against a dashboard this scenario could start and leave running.
dashboard status shows the dashboard status — Blocked-on the same long-running-process verb for the running half; the not-running half would assert a state no step arranged.
dashboard logs tails the dashboard logs, service mode only — Unrealizable in a sandbox: the logs come from the installed background service, which a sandbox must not install.
dashboard uninstall removes the background service — Unrealizable in a sandbox for the same reason: there is no machine service to remove.

the first dashboard run asks console or background service — Blocked-on the long-running-process verb: the question is answerable on a TTY, but every answer leaves a serving dashboard or an installed service behind.

claim `dashboard-violations-copy-fix-copies-the-prompt` (flow `read-a-violation-card-and-silence-its-rule`): The claim is about the SYSTEM CLIPBOARD holding the same text the expanded fix prompt shows. The web verb set is closed at navigate/click/fill/expect and its expectations read only the page's text, its address and an element's visibility — there is no clipboard channel. Asserting that the button relabels to `Copied!` would prove the button changed, not that anything was copied, which is exactly the assertion theater the corpus forbids. The fix-prompt EXPANSION milestone is proved immediately before it, so the comparison target exists the moment the vocabulary grows a clipboard read.

claim `dashboard-analytics-trend-change-is-red-up-green-down` (flow `read-the-analytics-of-a-run`): The claim is a COLOUR treatment (the delta drawn in red when up, green when down), carried on a class on the trend icon. A web expectation reads text, address and visibility — never computed style — so there is no honest observation. The delta VALUE is proved by the milestone beside it.

claim `dashboard-analytics-donut-slice-filters-the-list` (flow `read-the-analytics-of-a-run`): The donut is a recharts pie whose slices are `<path class="recharts-sector">` with no ARIA role, no accessible name, no `<title>` and no focusability (the chart's accessibility layer is not enabled). The locator vocabulary is role + accessible name by design, so there is no user-replayable way to click one slice. Recorded as a schema/markup gap rather than addressed with CSS.

claim `dashboard-analytics-selected-slice-pops-out` (flow `read-the-analytics-of-a-run`): Both halves are visual: an offset SVG sector and dimmed siblings. Neither the click (see above) nor the result is expressible in the web vocabulary.

claim `dashboard-analytics-severity-bar-filters-the-list` (flow `read-the-analytics-of-a-run`): Same markup case as the donut: the bars are `<path class="recharts-rectangle">` with no role and no name, and the per-severity axis ticks are SVG text that is not the click target. The chart's CONTENT (a bar per severity present, none for a severity that is not) is proved by the milestone beside it.

claim `dashboard-analytics-top-offenders-ranks-up-to-ten` (flow `read-the-analytics-of-a-run`): Not a vocabulary gap but a WORLD gap, and the more useful finding of the two: no deterministic rule attributes its finding to a service or module (every deterministic violation carries null service and module targets), and Top Offenders counts only attributed findings — so in any `--no-llm` world the table renders its empty state. Proving it needs either LLM-raised architecture findings or the supplied analysis-target the flow's starting state names; authoring `at most ten rows` against zero rows would pass vacuously.

claim `dashboard-analytics-offender-row-scopes-the-list` (flow `read-the-analytics-of-a-run`): Same world gap: with no attributed findings there is no offender row to click. (The row markup itself is fine — Top Offenders is a real table whose rows carry role `row` and a name — so this becomes expressible the moment the world has an attributed finding.)

claim `dashboard-graph-edges-on-hover-only` (flow `explore-the-architecture-graph`): The claim's content is what happens WHEN A NODE IS HOVERED. There is deliberately no hover verb (§ web-steps: no hover, no scroll, no keyboard), so the conditional half cannot be produced. The scenario still flips the control — that flip is what the remembered-in-the-browser milestone needs — but the flip alone is not the claim.

claim `dashboard-graph-hover-dims-untouched-edges` (flow `explore-the-architecture-graph`): Hover again, and a dimming treatment on top of it: two things the vocabulary cannot do (produce the hover) and cannot read (the computed opacity of an edge).

claim `dashboard-graph-curved-or-l-shaped-edges` (flow `explore-the-architecture-graph`): The observation is the SHAPE of the drawn edge path — SVG geometry. Nothing in text, address or visibility distinguishes a bezier from a step edge.

claim `dashboard-graph-animations-on-or-off` (flow `explore-the-architecture-graph`): Motion. A driver that reads text and takes screenshots has no honest observation of animation at all — this is the clearest case in the batch of a claim that must wait for a capability rather than be approximated.

claim `dashboard-graph-clicking-a-service-group-zooms-with-children` (flow `explore-the-architecture-graph`): LOCATOR: service-group nodes render as plain divs inside the graph library's wrapper, which carries role `group` with NO accessible name (and `group` takes no name from content), so the node cannot be addressed by the roles-and-labels policy. The database-node click is authored anyway because the doc's contradiction is the flow's most valuable step and the brief asked for it; doing the same twice would add a second locator failure without a second finding.

claim `dashboard-graph-clicking-empty-canvas-clears-and-fits` (flow `explore-the-architecture-graph`): LOCATOR and OBSERVATION both: empty canvas is the React Flow pane (role `application`, no accessible name) with nothing to name, and the result — no node selected, the whole graph back in view — is a class and a viewport transform.

claim `dashboard-files-names-colored-by-worst-severity` (flow `walk-files-flows-and-databases`): The tree applies severity as an inline `color` style and renders no severity text or attribute; the row itself is a `div` with no role. Colour is not readable by a text/address/visibility expectation.

claim `dashboard-files-folders-roll-up-counts-and-severity` (flow `walk-files-flows-and-databases`): Stronger than a vocabulary gap: the tree renders NO count text at all, per row or per folder (the count is computed in the component and never reaches the DOM), and the rolled-up severity is again colour only. There is nothing on the page to assert, in any vocabulary — a doc/product divergence worth reporting on its own.

claim `dashboard-files-gutter-bar-spans-the-finding-lines` (flow `walk-files-flows-and-databases`): The gutter marker is an imperatively built div with inline styles only — no role, no name, no text, no attribute carrying the line range. Both halves of the claim (the span and the colour) are style.

claim `dashboard-analytics-past-run-point-is-ringed` (flow `review-run-history-and-enter-diff-mode`): The ring is an SVG marker attribute on one point of the recharts trend line. No text, no name, no address distinguishes it; reading it would need an attribute or computed-style channel the web expectation does not have.

claim "the documented baseline setup sequence works" dismissed 2026-08-11 as doc drift: analyze has never written config.json; the doc's baseline git-add recipe is being corrected. See scenarios/decisions.json.

claim `dashboard-violations-code-hotspot-row-scopes-the-list` (flow `filter-the-violation-list`): blocked on an observation channel — the Code Hotspots ranking is computed client-side from the unordered `violations/summary` byFile map (no API returns the ranked list) and web steps have no capture channel, so against a SUPPLIED project the top hotspot row cannot be named by any locator. The seeded analytics flow proves the same behavior for its own doc (dashboard-analytics-hotspot-row-filters-the-list, passing). Clears when a web text-capture channel or a ranked-hotspots API exists (ledger G91).
